items.title: Chink Martin Interview, 1966-10-19
items.q: I ran into Pee Wee standing on the corner outside the club down there. And he had been with Al about two weeks at that time. I said, Pee Wee, how do you like playing with Al Hurt?

ctx.x: The clarinet player always did play the variations. I'll admit I did. But they do learn? They tried to fill in as much as they possibly could.

Can I digress for a moment, Bill, on this very point, getting kind of modern now. When Pete Fountain was Al Hurt's clarinet player and then he went out and got on Lawrence Welk and so on. He really never did come back to the band. And Pee Wee Spadalera went into Al Hurt's band. And I was walking down Bourbon Street to buy my paper, as I do many a night, and I ran into Pee Wee standing on the corner outside the club down there.
